title: Extensions of lisse native coefficient sheaves are lisse
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic absolute-value topology, and use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For any scheme $X$, let $B_X$ be the sheaf of locally finite continuous $\Omega$-valued functions: its sections on $U$ are continuous functions $|U|\to\Omega$ such that every point has an open neighbourhood on which the values span a finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-space. Restrictions are by precomposition. This is the coefficient construction used in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework], applied to $X$ itself. Write $\mathcal A_X=\operatorname{Mod}(B_X)$. Call an object lisse if it is pro-etale locally isomorphic to $B_U^{\oplus r_U}$ with $r_U$ a finite nonnegative integer, allowed to vary with the covering member $U$. Let $X$ be any scheme and let $0\to M\to E\to N\to0$ be a short exact sequence in $\mathcal A_X$ [def-sp-abelian]. If $M$ and $N$ are lisse, then $E$ is lisse. This assertion does not require a Noetherian hypothesis on $X$.
